_: Events that are NOT commits in this repository, and would otherwise be invisible on /history/.
_why: The timeline is built from this repo's git log, and this repo begins at 2026-09-04T00:36 with the first static site commit. Everything before that - the board, its gateway, the WhatsApp intake, the Apps Script deployments, the move off Google Sites - happened in the private working repo or in third-party consoles. A history that starts when the website starts tells the reader the work started when the website did.
_rule: Every entry cites where it can be checked. Nothing here links to a private repository, because a link a reader cannot open is worse than a citation they can at least verify with the owner. Entries are MEASURED from a commit, a deployment version or a dated record - none are written from memory.

events.subject: The working repository is created. Two commits, a README and a scaffold.
First revision of the shared-board gateway: append, read and time over HTTP, with a lock so two writers cannot interleave. Credentials in script properties, never in source.
The gateway, its clients and an architecture note go under version control. Deployment URLs stay out of the repo and are handed over out of band.
WhatsApp intake is wired through Pipedream: a webhook receives each message and writes it to the shared board as its own row.
A capture feeder and uploader ship, with retention limits by count and by age, so the folder cannot grow without bound.
The gateway gets a dual-secret rotation window, so a key can be replaced without a moment where writes are refused.
Three write endpoints are documented, along with the deploy traps that had already cost time.
An audit of the functions the page exposes to the browser finds four that should never have been callable. Guards added.
Version 13 deployed: the exposed-function guards are live and verified, not assumed.
The site goes down. DNS had moved off Google to another registrar and the name stopped resolving.

Back up 47 minutes later: www to the host, apex forwarding, and no redirect loop. The false relapse that followed turned out to be a local DNS cache, and that diagnosis was written down rather than remembered.
Deployment from the shell works for the first time, once the script API is enabled. Version 14 goes out without touching a browser.
Board writes become idempotent: deduplication inside the lock, so a retry cannot post the same row twice.
The outage root cause is corrected: a tag collision, not the thing first blamed. Two issues filed against the real fault.
A monitor goes live, then immediately produces a false alarm. Fixed the same hour by separating the signals and requiring two strikes before it speaks.
Visitors can sign in with Google: redirect flow, signed sessions. Identity is recorded; it grants nothing.
A page could show one identity while serving another's data. Never again: the page must say which identity it means.
The cutover off the old host takes the site down in browsers only, while every command-line check said it was fine. A certificate had not been issued yet.
The fleet gets a way to reach a person: a WhatsApp sender an agent can use when it is blocked, and a watchdog that can speak.
Inbound WhatsApp is picked up and answered, with questions shaped so they can be answered in one tap rather than a paragraph.
The WhatsApp media fetch is fixed. It had never actually run - the path existed and had never been exercised.

Two strings that only exist as test fixtures reach the live site and are taken off twice in one afternoon. A check that reads the test suite's own source and fails on any sentence it plants is added the same day.

Nine messages sent to the fleet by WhatsApp are found unread on the board. Inbound had always worked; nothing was reading the tag they arrive under. A watcher now reads it every 23 minutes and answers with a receipt that names which agent has it.
